q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance (Q3 FY2027 Revenue)

## (a) Time Left Until Resolution
Today is August 19, 2026. The earnings release is scheduled for Wednesday, August 26, 2026.
**Time left: 7 days**

## (b) Most Likely Outcome and Why

The question asks for NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release, specifically the revenue guidance they will provide for Q3 FY2027.

Key facts from the research:
- Consensus revenue for Q3 FY2027 is **$103.1 billion**
- Q2 FY2027 guidance was $91.0 billion ±2% (actual: ~$91.85 billion)
- NVIDIA typically provides guidance that is achievable but conservative
- The research explicitly states analysts will be watching whether Q3 guidance "meets or exceeds" the $103.1 billion consensus
- NVIDIA excludes China Data Center revenue from guidance due to regulatory restrictions
- The company has strong momentum with new products (Vera CPU) and market expansion

**Most likely outcome:** NVIDIA will provide Q3 FY2027 forward guidance around **$103-105 billion**, aligned with or slightly above consensus. This represents approximately 12-15% sequential growth from Q2, which is consistent with NVIDIA's historical seasonal patterns and current business momentum.

The consensus figure of $103.1 billion is likely well-informed by market participants and analyst discussions, and NVIDIA typically guides near or modestly above consensus to demonstrate confidence without excessive risk.

## (c) What Would Push the Value Lower?

- **Weaker than expected Q2 results** – if actual Q2 revenue came in below the $91.0B guidance range, momentum concerns could force lower Q3 guidance
- **Macro deterioration** – broader tech spending weakness or customer inventory corrections
- **Competitive pressures** – if AMD or other competitors gain significant market share
- **Geopolitical restrictions tightening** – further restrictions on China revenue or other markets
- **Supply chain disruptions** – component shortages limiting delivery capability
- **Conservative guidance strategy** – NVIDIA may guide lower than consensus to ensure beats and maintain investor confidence

Range expectation: Lower bound around **99.5-101 billion** (if guidance is conservative or headwinds emerge)

## (d) What Would Push the Value Higher?

- **Stronger than expected Q2 execution** – beating guidance by a wider margin
- **Vera CPU acceleration** – faster than anticipated adoption of new CPU products
- **Data center demand surge** – customers front-loading orders ahead of new AI model releases
- **Market share gains** – winning more of the AI training/inference market
- **Geographic expansion** – stronger than expected international growth offsetting China restrictions
- **Analyst upgrades ahead of earnings** – consensus moving higher before the call
- **Guidance raise strategy** – NVIDIA demonstrating exceptional confidence in new platforms

Range expectation: Upper bound around **105-108 billion** (if guidance is strong)

## (e) Base Rate or Historical Reference Values

**From the research provided:**
- Q2 FY2027 guidance was $91.0 billion
- Q3 FY2027 consensus estimate is $103.1 billion
- This represents ~13.3% sequential growth consensus expectation

**Sequential growth patterns:** NVIDIA historically shows seasonal patterns with Q3 (calendar Q2) typically stronger than Q2 due to summer-month server shipments. The 13% sequential growth implied by consensus is reasonable but not exceptional by NVIDIA's recent standards (the company has seen 26%+ sequential growth in prior years during AI boom periods).

Since the research explicitly mentions that "analysts will be watching whether NVIDIA's official Q3 guidance meets or exceeds" $103.1 billion, this is the key benchmark. NVIDIA typically guides conservatively to safely beat, so I expect guidance to be close to or slightly above consensus.

## Probability Distribution Reasoning

The range provided (99.5 to 115.5 billion) is quite wide, suggesting meaningful uncertainty. However:

- **Below $100B is unlikely** (10-15% probability) – would require significant negative surprise
- **$100-104B is most likely** (50-60% probability) – consensus-aligned guidance
- **$104-108B is possible** (25-35% probability) – moderately optimistic guidance
- **Above $108B is unlikely** (5-10% probability) – would require very strong confidence

Given NVIDIA's position as the dominant AI beneficiary, strong Q2 execution expected, and analyst consensus at $103.1B, I expect guidance near this figure with slight upside bias.

NVIDIA is expected to release its Q2 FY2027 earnings on Wednesday, August 26, 2026. The key focus for this release will be the forward guidance for Q3 FY2027 revenue [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/).

For Q2 FY2027, NVIDIA's guidance was $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%. This outlook explicitly excludes any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027/). Consensus estimates for Q2 FY2027 revenue are slightly higher at $91.85 billion [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/), [hudson-labs.com](https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/nvidia-q2-2027-earnings-preview-nvda-revenue-guidance-key-factors/).

The consensus revenue for Q3 FY2027 is currently $103.1 billion. Analysts will be watching whether NVIDIA's official Q3 guidance meets or exceeds this figure, and if the exclusion of China Data Center revenue persists [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/). CFO Colette Kress has stated that NVIDIA's new Vera CPU could open up a new $200 billion market, with an anticipated $20 billion in total CPU revenue this year [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027/).
